sentence: A 45-year-old man was resuscitated from a CPA after an acute coronary syndrome in public and transferred to the hospital with absence of reflexes except for cough and spontaneous breathing.
After the hypothermia protocol, the same examination persisted, with generalized cerebral edema observed in the cranial CT.
On the third day of admission, the family members were informed of the poor prognosis and spontaneously suggested donation.
They were informed of the need to wait until it progressed to brain death, which they accepted.
On the fifth day of admission, the same neurological examination continued.
The family expressed their desire not to wait for brain death, asking for the withdrawal of life support.
They were approached about donation through the LTSV and controlled asystole protocol, giving their consent.
He was transferred to the operating room for terminal extubation.
Asystole occurred 9 minutes after extubation and once death was certified, rapid laparotomy, cannulation and intraoperative cold perfusion were performed.
Both kidneys were explanted, with the lungs discarded by bronchoaspiration and the liver by TIC at the limit.
